properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-07, verbatim: "the backlog needs to be retired once and for all - I approve whatever decisions need to be made to make this action occur." This settles dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph, open since 2026-08-04 with five options and no choice, and it supersedes it.

THE CHOICE IS OPTION (a) — ROUTE EACH ROW TO THE TYPE IT ALREADY IS — and it is only available now because the one category that had no home was given one. dec:defects-are-temporal-facts (accepted 2026-08-06) closed it: a defect found by USING a built capability is a TemporalFact with fact_type "defect". So all four categories the 2026-08-04 taxonomy identified now have a destination:

  (i)   a defect against a shipped capability  -> TemporalFact, fact_type "defect", basis "measured",
        HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT from the node it indicts, VALID_TO set when fixed
  (ii)  unbuilt work                            -> a Capability at `planned` behind a Requirement
  (iii) an open design question                 -> a `proposed` Decision
  (iv)  a discovered limit                      -> a Constraint or a DesignRule

OPTION (d) IS EXPLICITLY NOT TAKEN. Deriving a markdown backlog from the graph was the fallback that kept the file alive as a projection; "retired once and for all" is a stronger instruction than that, and dec:views-are-projections already covers rendering if anyone later wants a view. The file is DELETED, and its history stays in git where deleted files live.

THE MEASURED SCOPE, taken 2026-08-07 rather than carried from the 2026-08-04 note: docs/backlog.md is 3,356 lines / 589,326 bytes / 217 distinct BL ids. 129 open rows under "Next up", 9 under "Bigger threads", plus a "Closed" section that is already only short pointers to the CHANGELOG and a "Deliberate deferrals" section. 22 other files reference it, including AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, COORD.md and README.md, and CLAUDE.md names it as one of the three things to read at session start — so retiring the file is not finished until those pointers are too.

⭐ THE FAILURE MODE THIS DECISION MUST NOT PRODUCE, quoted from the decision it supersedes because it is the whole risk: "A row moved in as one long `description` rebuilds backlog.md inside the graph with worse ergonomics and no gain — and that failure would be invisible, because it would look like progress." So a row is migrated only when it becomes STRUCTURE: the node it bears on named by an EDGE, what was measured in a TYPED property, and whether it is still true carried by a status or a temporal bound. The prose hangs off that as explanation. A migration that produces 138 nodes of narrative and no edges has failed while appearing to succeed, and the honest test is whether the loop can see the result — not whether the file got shorter.

WHAT IS STILL OWED AND IS NOT SOLVED BY THIS. dec:defects-are-temporal-facts says it in its own words: nothing in the LOOP reads defect facts yet. `statement` is fulltext so search_design finds them, but `loop_status` does not count open defects — measured again today, and it does not. So a migrated defect is DISCOVERABLE, not SURFACED. Retiring the file therefore trades a document nobody queries for nodes the loop does not yet count, and that reader is the next increment. Recorded here so the trade is a choice rather than a discovery.

CLOSED ROWS ARE NOT MIGRATED. The "Closed" section is already only stable-id pointers into the CHANGELOG, and a finished item's value is history that git holds. Migrating them would import 100+ nodes that indict nothing and are true of nothing.
properties.name: The backlog is retired: every open row becomes the node type it already was, and docs/backlog.md is deleted rather than derived
properties.rationale: Accepted rather than left `proposed` because Anthony's approval was explicit, unprompted and general ("whatever decisions need to be made"), which is the standard dec:three-party-checks sets — the human decides, and here they did, in advance and in writing. He had already stated the preference on 2026-08-04 ("I wanted to stop using the BL... instead, I wanted everything in the graph") and it sat unchosen for three days while the file grew. The cost of leaving it open is measured on the superseded node: 6 of 8 rows filed in one session referenced by zero graph nodes, and four things re-derived in that same session that were already written down. The falsifiable test from dec:what-lives-where applies to reflow2 itself and it has been failing it: if reflow2 works, reflow2 would not need a 589 KB markdown backlog.
